differences.what: massing: the draft's generic block is now the plate's house: a narrow red brick front two storeys over a stone basement under a steep slated hip with a street dormer, its long north flank running back past a round tower to steep-gabled half-storey ranges and a two-storey garage; the two tall stacks, the tower, the dormer and the front's corners lie within about 15-25 px of the plate (16 px RMS on the fitted points)

the street hip's pitch: the plate and the 1919 programme plate draw the front block's roof steeper than T-3279's 45 degrees; T-3280 built it at 52 degrees, read off the programme plate's camera (the hip's apex at about 15.9 m), the stacks' rise lowered by as much so their tops stay at about 17.4 m

the broad bow across the front's north part, which the plate shows as the wall and eave sweeping round from the north corner: built as a K08 bow, 6.0 m on its chord and 1.0 m out, where the 1911 sheet draws the front swelling 0.8 m forward

the front's north corner: the plate sweeps the wall and the main eave round it on a curve and the 1911 sheet cuts it back about 0.85 by 1.2 m; T-3314 rounds it on 1.0 m from grade to the eave (K01's round_corner carried to the eave): the stone basement, its coping and the three pale belts run round it with the red brick between them, and the soffit, fascia, bed moulding and gutter follow the curve, the slate turning it as a quarter cone; through this camera the eave now curves round beside the tower where the plate's does

the bow is carried up to the eave in the plate, the main cornice running round it; T-3313 carries it up: its upper storey rises to the cornice's bed (8.6 m) and the bed moulding, the house's soffit and fascia run round its plan at the main eave's line (K08's eaves.cornice, T-2472), its nearly flat cap dying into the hip; through this camera the eave sweeps out round the bow where the plate's does, and the bow stands 0.2 m further south (s 4.1 m) to leave the corner bracket room

the round tower: the plate takes it about 2 m higher than T-3279's cone and broader-topped; T-3280 carried it up a fourth, windowless 1.9 m band to a flat top at 14.0 m under K08's nearly flat tin cap, its eaves the heavy edge, which this camera reads within about 1 m of the plate's top (14.9 m) and the 1919 programme plate's at 13.7 m; a parapet's own coping and mouldings are not drawn

the corner block's street face (T-3354, third run): the two-light stone-mullioned window this plate draws in each storey of the 3.1 m face the middle range stands out north of the front block, where the record had bare brick, is built (rear_wings.mullioned, the kit's paired flat sash under a stone lintel); through this camera the built pair lands about 17 px (about 0.5 m) right of the plate's, as the block's quoined corner itself does, so against the corner it stands where the plate puts it

the corner block's north face (T-3354, third run, read again): in each storey this plate draws a group of three narrow pale lights under one head, mullioned, along the face west of the quoined corner, where the record has two single sashes at s 2.0 and 5.0 m; the face is about 45 px across here and the plate's corner stands about 17 px off the build's, so the group's place and span along it (about s 0-4 m by this camera) are not read closely enough to build; a three-light group is the plates' (the 1919 programme plate draws the same)

the steep gables over the rear ranges: the plate draws three, stepped and finialled at their peaks; T-3337 carries both ranges' gables up in a stone coping with kneelers and a turned finial at each apex; the small pinnacled dormers between the gables, on the rear range's slope facing the street: all three plates draw two, and T-3354 builds them (rear_wings.rear_range.roof.dormers, k01_wing_dormers): at v -3.85 and -2.3 m, their faces 0.3 m in from the range's wall line over the middle range's flat end, each a 1.0 m face with one tall light under a 60-degree stone-coped gable to its finial, a pinnacle at each edge; through this camera both land on the plate's two within about 10 px

the street dormer: the plate's is broad, three lights under its gable; T-3280 built it 3.3 m wide with three lights (K01's `sash.at_m`) where T-3279's carried one sash; T-3301 carried its gable up in a stone coping with kneelers and a finial (K01's `dormer.coping`), as the plate's pale gable and the 2004 photograph show

the entrance at the stoop's head: the plate shows an arched opening beside the south neighbour; T-3305 builds K07's round-arched entrance (1.3 by 3.3 m, stone ring and keystone, a pair of leaves under a fanlight), and through this camera its round head stands at the stoop's head at the front's south end, where the plate's arch is

stone belts and dressings: the plate shows a pale stone basement and pale courses across the brick; T-3305 lays the stone basement to the principal floor round the front, the bow, the tower and the north flank, and three stone belts across the brick (under the principal sills, at the second floor, under the chamber sills) on the front and carried round the north flank; through this camera the basement and the second-floor belt read across the bow and the front's return where the plate's pale bands do
windows: their count and places along the front and the flank are the kit's, not read (the plate is too coarse and the trees hide the lower storey)

a second, smaller street dormer near the front's south end, one light under its own gable, and the stack rising behind the street dormers at the front block's south side: T-3301 built both (`dormer.also` at v 8.05 m, 1.6 m wide; a third stack at u 14.5 m, v 7.5 m), and through this camera the small dormer's gable stands at the front's south end against the south neighbour's mansard edge and the stack behind the broad dormer, each within about 1 m of the plate
colour: the brick's red, the stone's tone and the slate are read from later photographs and the trade's materials; the plate is monochrome

the south neighbour (1923, the mansard at the plate's right edge), the street trees, the lamp post and the iron fence's pattern: not part of this record (the fence is K11's scroll band, its pattern unreadable)

the quoins and courses on the north flank's ranges the programme plate shows (T-3353 quoins both ranges' north-east corners and carries the main block's three stone courses across them, off that plate); this plate shows the flank too obliquely and under trees to read them

the rear ranges' gables against all three Gatlin plates (T-3354): the MIDDLE range's gable now stands back 1.6 m from its north end over a flat deck (roof.flat_end) and is pitched 60 degrees, where it rose 50 degrees off the north wall; through the 1912, 1913 and 1919 cameras its finial now lands on the plates' highest gable within about 5 px across and 8 px up (it stood 25-30 px left and 30-60 px under). The REAR range's apex still stands about 20-35 px (1-2 m) left of the plates' second gable, the same way in all three, and the plates do not show its plan; re-cutting it waits on a reading that reconciles the 1911 trace with the plates (L-k01-1919-garage-gable-3354, L-k01-1919-range-dormers-3354)

the third, smaller gable the plates draw at the flank's far end, coped and finialled as the ranges' are: T-3354 roofs the garage under a slated gable facing the flank, pitched 54 degrees to an apex at 15.7 m, with the ranges' stone coping, kneelers and 0.6 m finial (where it was flat in tin); through this camera its apex lands on the plate's third gable within about 15 px

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
